Register a data-source adapter

Source: R/registry.R
register_source.Rd

Adds a source adapter to the registry. Enforces the data-collector role's free-only rule: an adapter that does not reach a free source is refused.

Usage

register_source(
  id,
  fun,
  package,
  free,
  description = "",
  extent = NULL,
  batch = NULL
)

Arguments

id

Character scalar. Unique source id (used as source in geo_point_request()).

fun

A function function(request, retrieved_at) returning a geo_point_series.

package

Character scalar. The upstream package the adapter needs (declared in Suggests; checked at collect time).

free

Logical scalar. Must be TRUE – the free-only role rule.

description

Character scalar. One-line description.

extent

Optional numeric c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in WGS84 giving the source's valid spatial extent, or NULL for a global source. A request outside a declared extent is refused by collect_point() rather than silently returning an out-of-coverage value (Independent Oracle Principle: an Australia-only source must not be queried over Argentina).

batch

Optional function function(requests, retrieved_at) that answers many requests for this source in one upstream call. It returns a list of the same length as requests, each element a geo_point_series or a refusal. collect_points() uses it for raster sources, where one file read serves every point. NULL (the default) means requests are answered one at a time by fun.

Value

Invisibly, the registered id.

Examples

toy_adapter <- function(request, retrieved_at) {
  dt <- data.frame(date = request$start, variable = "toy", value = 1)
  new_geo_point_series(
    dt, lon = request$lon, lat = request$lat,
    source = "toy", source_version = "1.0", license = "CC0",
    retrieved_at = retrieved_at, call = "toy_adapter()"
  )
}
register_source("toy", toy_adapter, package = "base", free = TRUE,
                 description = "Illustrative in-memory adapter")
"toy" %in% list_sources()$id
#> [1] TRUE
